A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSD research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original RSD benchmark results, loss and timestep ablations, inference measurements and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds experiments with models trained on higher-resolution LSDIR images.

M1.justification: The student/fake-ResShift design, distillation objective, multistep training, single-step inference and LPIPS/GAN losses are retained. Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged apart from notation and cross-references.

E1.justification: Appendix E extends the authors' training experiments from ImageNet to LSDIR, previously discussed as OSEDiff's training data. The natural-image super-resolution task and evaluation datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 Table 16 adds one-step AddSR comparisons on the existing DIV2K-Val, DRealSR and RealSR crop benchmarks. AddSR was discussed but not evaluated in v2; the earlier comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a separate protocol: train a ResShift teacher on 512×512 LSDIR crops for 300,000 iterations, then distill it with RSD and SinSR using their retained hyperparameters. The original 256×256 training setup and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E tests whether RSD's advantage over SinSR persists after changing both training data and resolution, using Table 14 and Figure 5. This does not isolate resolution alone. The original timestep/loss ablations and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added training-iteration information does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The matched original benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. New Table 14 reports, for example, MUSIQ 64.987 for RSD versus 59.478 for SinSR under the added 512×512/LSDIR training condition. Table 16 adds AddSR scores across three benchmarks.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly adds the assumption that agreement between the teacher and generator-trained ResShift implies agreement between generated and training-data distributions (Eq. 6). Proposition 3.1, its proof and the appendix trajectory-KL derivation are retained; the additional gradient discussion explains the existing argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about one-step distillation, perceptual quality, fidelity and computational efficiency. The additional experiments support these contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix E qualifies higher-resolution performance through the untuned teacher and remaining no-reference metric gap to OSEDiff. Section 4.2 and Appendix C add a training-efficiency explanation based on avoiding SinSR's full teacher rollout while requiring fake-model updates.

D1.justification: Appendices C, E and F add SinSR training-cost information, the higher-resolution teacher training recipe and explicit loss implementation details. Dataset-license disclosures also change, including RealSR-V3's listed license and omission of RealSet65's license entry. Existing code/data access links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3.6 and Appendix F expand positioning against the already cited ADD/AddSR methods. DreamFusion/SDS and U-Net references are added, while Dong et al. (2016) and Luhman and Luhman (2021) are removed. Existing VSD/SiD/FGM/IBMD relationships are retained.

P1.justification: Much of the introduction, related work and experimental narrative is rewritten and compressed, with systematic DM terminology and explicit baseline names replacing citation-only mentions. The exposition gains Section 3.6, an expanded appendix roadmap and an LLM-usage statement.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 5 and Tables 14–16, splits dataset sources and licenses into separate tables, and reflows existing displays. Original visual examples are retained; one failure-case figure is downsampled, and later figures are renumbered.

improvement.justification: Appendix E partly addresses v2's acknowledged training-resolution mismatch with OSEDiff through additional LSDIR/512×512 experiments and explicit qualifications about their results. Appendix F supplies a previously missing AddSR comparison. These strengthen empirical support and clarify applicability, although higher-resolution validation covers only RealSR and the central proof and original results remain unchanged.
